title: The Day a 14-Inch Drill Bit Swallowed an Entire Lake

basis.note: median of recent videos; learning gated until day 5

segments.narration: A fourteen-inch drill bit swallowed an entire freshwater lake. In 1980, workers on Louisiana's Lake Peigneur hit a subterranean wall they didn't expect.
Water began spiraling downward, opening a roaring fifty-foot whirlpool in minutes. The drill rig tipped over, snapping its moorings, and disappeared under the surface.
The whirlpool swallowed eleven barges and 65 acres of surrounding land.
The drill bit had accidentally punctured an underground salt mine operating directly beneath the water. As fresh water hit the salt, it dissolved the mine shafts instantly, creating a mega-drain.

The drain pulled in the nearby canal, reversing its flow to fill the crater with ocean water. Amazingly, all fifty-five workers escaped without a single injury, leaving behind Louisiana’s deepest, saltwater lake.

verdicts.claim: A 14-inch drill bit punctured the bed of Lake Peigneur in Louisiana in 1980.
verdicts.note: The reference confirms a 14-inch drill assembly punctured the lake bed/salt mine at Lake Peigneur in Louisiana on November 20, 1980.

verdicts.claim: A massive whirlpool formed on Lake Peigneur, pulling down a drilling rig.
verdicts.note: The reference states that the drill hole created a vortex that swallowed the drilling platform.

verdicts.claim: The whirlpool swallowed eleven barges and fifty acres of surrounding land.
verdicts.note: The reference states that the sinkhole swallowed 65 acres of surrounding terrain, not fifty acres.
verdicts.correction: The whirlpool swallowed eleven barges and 65 acres of surrounding land.

verdicts.claim: The drill bit accidentally hit an active salt mine underneath the lake bed, dissolving the salt shafts.
verdicts.note: The reference confirms that the drill assembly pierced an active salt mine beneath the lake, dissolving the salt pillars supporting the ceiling.

verdicts.claim: The disaster reversed the flow of the Delcambre Canal and created Louisiana's deepest saltwater lake with zero human fatalities.
verdicts.note: The reference confirms that the flow of the Delcambre Canal reversed, there were no human deaths, and the resulting salty/brackish lake became the deepest lake in Louisiana at 200 feet.

candidates.why: Highlights the massive environmental consequence of a small mistake.
